title: GHG emission reduction potential of EU-related maritime transport and its impacts.
description: The contract should lead to the identification of the marginal abatement costs in the sector and the no-regret GHG emission reduction potential from maritime transport up until 2030. No-regret means that the costs associated with the emission reduction, such as investment costs, operational costs or carbon costs, remain lower than the savings, especially fuel savings, generated by the emission reduction.In particular, the contract should define the in-sector cost-effective GHG emission reduction, as well as the overall cost-effective contribution from maritime transport to tackle climate change, including through the purchase of offsets/allowances from other sectors.The contract should also carry out a sensitivity analysis underlying the relevant parameters leading to a variation of GHG emissions from maritime transport. In particular, impacts of changes in GDP and its geographical distribution, fuel price variations and improvement of design and operational energy efficiency should be clearly pointed out.

title: Strengthening independent monitoring of GHG emissions from land activities for publishing, comparing and reconciling estimates.
description: Strengthening independent monitoring of GHG emissions from land activities for publishing, comparing and reconciling estimates: the general objective of this contract is to develop a proof of concept for publicly available, comprehensive, global, spatial information systems on land cover, land emissions, land use and associated trends. Such systems would be intended to softly reconcile estimates and underlying methodologies, to facilitate dissemination of information, to identify hotspots of land emissions and to prioritize effective and efficient climate action in AFOLU, at global scale (mitigation and risk management). This effort shall contribute to building capacities, trust and shared understanding between all parties preparing their contribution to the Climate Agreement 2015, with a view to becoming fully operational by 2020.

title: Support Contract for an Impact Assessment for Amending Regulation (EC) No 1005/2009 on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer
description: In 2017, the European Commission launched an evaluation of Regulation (EC) No 1005/2009 on substances that deplete the ozone layer (the Regulation). Building on the results of the evaluation, this contract aims to provide a timely and high quality assessment report supporting the commission in the impact assessment for amending the regulation. The Impact Assessment will set out a range of policy options to achieve the specific and operational objectives and analyse the likely economic, social, climate and environmental impacts of these options, in line with the commission's better regulation guidelines. This will include, among other activities, carrying out a broad consultation on the possible amendment of the regulation and the various options, in order to listen closely to stakeholders and citizens in the development of EU legislation on ozone layer protection.

title: Refactoring and Improving VECTO Software for the Next Amendment of Commission Regulation (EU) 2017/2400
description: VECTO is at the core of the system to determine CO2 emissions and energy consumption from heavy-duty vehicles (HDVs). Is the crucial tool for the implementation and development of CO2 emission standards for HDVs, which contribute to the 'European Green Deal' and the backbone of HDVs certification, therefore an essential tool to ensure the implementation and revision of the HDVs CO2 emission standards for various types of vehicles (conventional, hybrids, electric, etc). It has to be updated regularly in order to capture all latest technologies and developments in the automotive sector. This contract aims to further develop and refactor the tool's software and bring up to a certain level all features needed for the next amendment of Commission Regulation (EU) 2017/2400.

title: Exploring expansion of NER 300 system.
description: The NER 300 programme is one of the largest funding schemes for the demonstration of low-carbon technologies at commercial scale and contributes to the implementation of a number of EU energy and climate policies and strategies.The European Council asked in its conclusions on the 2030 climate and energy policy framework that ‘the existing NER 300 facility be renewed, including for carbon capture and storage and renewables, with the scope extended to low-carbon innovation in industrial sectors and the initial endowment increased to 400 000 000 allowances (NER 400).’The objectives of this tender are twofold. On the one hand, the contractor will analyse how the modalities of the NER 300 Decision have performed. On the other hand, the contractor will compare where possible with alternatives, suggest updates to the requirements where necessary, complement them to match the directions given by the European Council and conclude on the best approach in the expanded NER 300 Decision and related documents. This will also include specific tasks for the industry part of the expanded NER 300 programme.

title: Study on the Risks of Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing and Fraud Inherent in the Union Registry and Data Protection Impact Assessment
description: The EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) is a cornerstone of the European Union's policy to combat climate change and is its key tool for reducing industrial greenhouse gas emissions. It covers more than 11 000 power stations, industrial plants and aircraft operators in 31 countries. The Union Registry and the European Union Transaction Log (EUTL) track the ownership of allowances by recording the amounts owned in the accounts and the transactions between accounts.The general objective of this study is to assess the risks related to fraud, money laundering and terrorist financing inherent in the EU ETS and the Union Registry, to propose mitigation measures for the identified risks and to perform a data protection impact assessment in case the implementation of the proposed measures would require that.

title: Study on climate finance reporting, including methodological issues, producing overview information and assessing emerging requirements.
description: The EU Member States and the European Commission see transparency in climate finance as key to building trust. Currently, the EU and its Member States have obligations to report on financial support provided both under the international UNFCCC framework and under the EU framework, namely Regulation (EU) No 525/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 21.5.2013 on a mechanism for monitoring and reporting greenhouse gas emissions and for reporting other information at national and Union level relevant to climate change and repealing Decision No 280/2004/EC (Monitoring Mechanism Regulation (MMR)). The study should provide support for assessing and aggregating the information received through the various reporting obligations, also improving methodological approaches. Furthermore, it will be important for the EU and its Member States to develop their approach to climate finance in the light of ongoing work streams under various processes (e.g. OECD, MDBs) and in view of the role of climate finance in the future Climate Agreement. The contract also involves tasks relating to the developments in these areas.

title: Study on mapping the development of the international carbon market.
description:
The objective of this study is to map out possible scenario(s) for the development of the global carbon market in the period 2020–2030 in light of the Paris Agreement and in particular its Article 6. Specifically, the study is to:
1. identify existing and planned carbon units/offset credits, including (voluntary) offset programmes around the globe;
2. assess the carbon units/offset credits identified under task 1 in terms of climate mitigation; and
3. elaborate and assess different options for the transfer, accounting and tracking of internationally transferred mitigation outcomes under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement.

title: Modelling, Projecting and Tracking Emissions Reduction Pathways
description: Many emerging and developing countries point to the need for capacity building for transparency and for modelling needed for the development of climate strategies, policies and NDCs. The first and second iteration of Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) submitted to the UNFCCC, suggest that many countries would benefit from improved data and modelling, to better understand the potential for domestic climate action and policies and for evidence-based policymaking. This contract intends to alleviate a part of this gap by supporting experts based in relevant institutes in selected developing countries to enhance the national capacity to model climate policy, project national greenhouse gas emissions, prepare targets and estimate the impacts of domestic policies and measures, as well as to track progress towards the achievement of their NDCs.The contract should also support experts’ participation in meetings that are of interest to the modelling community.

description: Model-based economic analysis is important for policy preparation and essential to achieve the EU objectives on climate change. This cannot be limited to representing the EU economy. Climate policies in the EU also depend on global developments led by the new climate change agreement under the UNFCCC and at national level. This contract should give access to a broad set of state of the art modelling tools that can assess climate policies on global scale and in major partner countries. This contract should be dedicated to improving the performance of the global modelling tools that can inform EU climate policy-making and to improving the understanding of policies put in place in third countries, it should therefore also include data gathering on policies in place or planned in partner countries.

title: Contratto quadro di servizi relativo alla qualità dei combustibili venduti e utilizzati nell'Unione europea e altrove.
description: Contratto quadro di servizi relativo alla qualità e alle emissioni di gas serra prodotte nel ciclo di vita dei combustibili liquidi venduti e utilizzati nell'Unione europea e altrove. Le emissioni prodotte dalla combustione dei carburanti per i trasporti contribuiscono all'inquinamento atmosferico e hanno un impatto negativo sulla salute, l'ambiente e il clima. Le emissioni sono state quantificate nella strategia tematica sull'inquinamento dell'aria pubblicata nel 2005 [COM(2005) 446] e nel percorso verso un'economia competitiva a basse emissioni di carbonio per il 2050 [COM(2011) 112]. Il ruolo dei combustibili liquidi e il loro contributo all'inquinamento dell'aria e alle emissioni di gas serra sono stati riconosciuti nel diritto comunitario che ha stabilito requisiti minimi di qualità e obiettivi di riduzione per una gamma di diversi biocombustibili e combustibili derivati dal petrolio.Relativamente alla qualità dei carburanti esiste un significativo corpus legislativo dell'UE:1) la direttiva 1998/70/CE come modificata disciplina la qualità della benzina e del diesel venduti nell'UE. Comprende un'ampia gamma di parametri sulla qualità dei combustibili che incidono sulle emissioni nell'aria. Inoltre la direttiva disciplina il tenore di zolfo dei combustibili utilizzati da macchine mobili non stradali e navi adibite alla navigazione interna, trattori agricoli o forestali e imbarcazioni da diporto;2) la direttiva 1999/32/CE come modificata disciplina il tenore di zolfo di alcuni combustibili liquidi inclusi gli oli combustibili pesanti, i gasoli (gasoli da riscaldamento) e i carburanti marini quali gli oli combustibili residui e i distillati marini.Oltre alla legislazione esistente ci sono un certo numero di attività in corso che potrebbero avere implicazioni sulla qualità e le emissioni di gas serra dei combustibili venduti e utilizzati nell'UE: 1) il Consiglio e il Parlamento europeo hanno richiesto che la Commissione presenti una relazione e, se appropriato, proponga un emendamento alla direttiva 98/70 sull'impatto del cambiamento indiretto di destinazione dei terreni sulle emissioni di gas serra dei biocombustibili; 2) il Consiglio e il Parlamento europeo hanno richiesto che la direttiva 98/70 venga riesaminata nel 2014 con l'obiettivo, tra gli altri, di rivedere gli obiettivi sui gas serra; 3) la Commissione ha presentato una proposta per modificare la direttiva 1999/32 [COM(2011) 439] nel luglio 2011. L'obiettivo dei lotti del presente bando di gara è quello di prestare servizi capaci di rispondere a esigenze relative alla legislazione europea riguardante i combustibili per i trasporti. Il lavoro comprenderà analisi tecniche ed economiche sulla qualità dei combustibili inclusa l'analisi ambientale e delle emissioni di gas serra prodotte nel ciclo di vita. Il primo e il secondo lotto affronteranno rispettivamente gli aspetti tecnici dei combustibili fossili e dei biocombustibili, inclusi gli aspetti microeconomici associati. Il terzo lotto affronterà gli aspetti macroeconomici dei combustibili fossili e dei biocombustibili.

title: Support to the Energy Union governance process, including for the integrated national energy and climate plans - technical and process support to Member States.
description:
The aim of this service contract is to support the timely delivery of draft and final integrated national energy and climate plans of the Member States as part of the Energy Union governance. It will help Member States to prepare both the draft and final national plans according to the process, timeline and template detailed in the proposed Regulation on the Governance of the Energy Union of 30.11.2016 and other supporting documents. Consultations on the plans are required domestically, with other Member States as well as with the Commission.
The nature of the practical support work is described in the technical specifications. A focus is on Member States who ask for Commission assistance due to technical or administrative capacity constraints with respect to certain elements of the national plan preparation.

title: Interactions between Climate Action and Defence
description:
The objective of the study is to analyse how EU climate action and defence policy interact in the context of Russia’s aggression, by identifying synergies, trade-offs and risks. It aims to:
•	assess how the defence sector can contribute to EU climate goals (mitigation, resilience, nature restoration and dual-use clean technologies), 
•	examine how climate policies can contribute to and impact on defence capabilities and readiness, the defence industry, build public resilience against hybrid threats, and budgetary priorities.
The study is intended to provide evidence for aligning rearmament and defence readiness with EU climate neutrality and resilience objectives and aligning the design of climate policies with defence needs.

title: Advancing Climate Finance for Global Transition Pathways Towards Carbon Neutrality and Climate Resilient Development
description:
Achieving the transition towards carbon-neutral and climate-resilient development necessitates a comprehensive understanding of the financial needs, targeted investment areas, and the deployment of effective financial instruments on a global scale. Moreover, reforming the international financial architecture is crucial to facilitate and support this transition.
The action should explore these critical dimensions of climate finance, including the identification of tools to monitor climate financial flows (public and private, international and domestic) as a foundation for evidence-based decision-making. The action should cover the following elements at global level with differentiation by geographic area with a focus on SIDS and LDCs: 1) Identification of Financial Needs for Climate Transition 2) Targeted Areas for Investment 3) Financial Instruments and Mechanisms 4) Reforming the International Financial Architecture 5) Monitoring Climate Financial Flows 6) Mobilizing Private Sector Investment.

The main objective of this (recurrent) project is to support the Commission and Member States in the further implementation of harmonized and cost-effective EU ETS Monitoring, Reporting Verification and Accreditation (MRVA), during 2026-2028. 

Specific objectives are to:
- Provide Secretariat support to the EU ETS Compliance Forum maintaining an effective platform for discussion and cooperation between Member States and the Commission and the well-functioning of EU ETS MRVA
- Provide support to the Commission concerning the maintenance of MRVA guidance, templates and other tools published by the Commission in support of the MRR and AVR.
- Provide additional support in relation to ad hoc technical enquiries on EU ETS MRVA issues
- Attendance to the TWG MRVA, CCC, and COM meetings

description:
We propose to launch a new contract with the aim of providing the Commission with assistance in the assessment of applications for new/changed allocations. The contractor will be required to carry out compliance checks of the applications received from the Commission based on a pre-agreed methodology. The contractors should give their technical input in the form of report to the Commission, which then decides on each application.
The contract will also contain a Helpdesk facility which is a service offered to Member States and which is highly useful and well appreciated by the competent authorities.

title: Modelling, projecting and tracking emissions reduction pathways in light of the second Global Stocktake by 2028
description:
The IPCC 6th Assessment Report emphasizes the urgent need to reduce greenhouse gas emissions this decade to keep global warming within 1.5 degrees above pre-industrial levels. This was highlighted by the first Global Stocktake (GST) in 2023, which emphasised that limiting global warming to 1.5°C with no or limited overshoot requires deep, rapid and sustained reductions in emissions of 43% reduction in emissions by 2030 and 60% by 2035 compared to 2019 levels, aiming for net zero CO2 emissions by 2050 and that mitigation efforts embedded within the wider development context can increase the pace, depth and breadth of emissions reductions. 

As we reach the midpoint of this critical decade for climate action, substantial efforts are required to meet the Paris Agreement goals. The period for this project will see the submission of new Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) for 2035 by parties to the Paris agreement, the IPCC’s 7th Assessment report, and the second Global Stocktake in 2028. The second GST will also assess how national action is closing the ambition and implementation gap towards limiting warming to 1.5 degrees.

This project aims to enhance the capacity of emerging economies to model GHG emissions and pathways, to improve tracking of progress towards domestic and global targets and to support the analysis and development of domestic targets, policies and measures to cut net emissions. By supporting experts and young professionals in developing countries and emerging economies it will enhance national capacity for modelling, reporting, and transparency.
This activity will facilitate knowledge exchange and best-practices between experts from the EU and other emerging, and developing countries and promote the drafting and publishing of relevant papers and reports to inform policy makers, and contributions to multi-lateral or international events including for climate negotiations and the second global stocktake. 

The project will be organised in a lean and efficient manner, allowing for flexibility in both the participation of stakeholders as well the selection of topics to be covered as to respond to climate policy developments as the project progresses. The project should have the capacity to respond to evolving demands and while being adaptive, propose regions or countries to engage with, where a high impact can be achieved with local partners. Structured around 4-6 in-person workshops over four years, 3-4 workshops will focus on modeling topics and 2-3 on MRV-related topics, with some addressing both.Each workshop will concentrate on a key climate action topic, bringing together scientists and stakeholders to produce scientific papers, reports, or follow-up projects to improve data quality and mitigation models.

The project will support collaboration among stakeholders, enabling capacity building and publishing outputs It will also create opportunities for young professionals in climate policy modeling and transparency through dedicated summer schools and seminars during the workshops. By building capacity, networks, and collaborations, participants will enhance their work through joint development. The selected tenderer has the capacity to deliver these tasks, both logistically and by steering the content development. 

Globally scoped, the project will engage experts in key countries for climate action and ensure workshops are held in various regions to maximize participation, especially where capacity development is most needed. The project will support the EU’s climate diplomacy.

title: Support for the review by the Commission concerning the implementation of ICAO’s CORSIA, and for Commission reports on certain types of flights, social impacts, and air connectivity of islands, remote territories and Iceland
description:
Provide for support for the revision of the ETS Directive for aviaiton

This call for tender requests analytical services for the review by the Commission concerning implementation by third countries of the International Civil Aviation Organization’s (ICAO) measure ‘Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation’ (CORSIA), as required by Article 28b (2) of Directive 2003/87/EC (hereinafter, "the Directive"), and including Article 25a(7) and Article 30(8).
It also requests analysis on environmental and climate impacts, and ways to reduce those, of short-haul flights, private- and business jet flights, as defined in Article 30(8)(a) and (b) of the Directive, and as required in Article 30(8). It also requests analysis of the social impacts of this Directive and connectivity, as required by Article 30(8)(c) and (d), the latter should also take into account Iceland.

All sectors of the economy, including international aviation, need to contribute to reduce greenhouse gas emissions so that we can comply with our commitment to the temperature goals of the Paris Agreement. title: Support for the evaluation of the EU emissions trading system (EU ETS) and the Market Stability Reserve (MSR) and for the 2026 review of the EU ETS and MSR
description:
The general objective of this contract is to support DG CLIMA in the evaluation of the EU ETS and the MSR, and in the review of certain elements due in 2026, by providing timely and high-quality input for supporting the Commission in drafting its own evaluation report and an impact assessment, in an almost parallel manner, in line with the Commission's Better Regulation Guidelines. 
The three specific objectives of this support contract are: (1) Support the Commission in drafting an “evaluation staff working document”, in particular assessing the effectiveness, relevance, efficiency, coherence and EU added value of the selected aspects of the ETS Directive and of the MSR Decision, as well as identifying areas of further action in this policy area in view of current and future climate change objectives. The selected aspects are: (i) Carbon leakage protection measures for non-CBAM sectors; and (ii) MSR in respect of ETS1. In addition, the consultant may be asked to carry out ad-hoc tasks related to the assessment of other interconnected elements that are to be included in the evaluation. (2) Support the Commission in drafting an “Impact Assessment staff working document" for revising selected aspects of the ETS Directive and the MSR Decision, by setting out a range of policy options and providing the evidence base for and the impacts of each option on the following topics: (i) MSR; (ii) negative emissions; (iii) accounting and double counting of non-permanent CCU; (iv) municipal waste incineration and other waste management processes; (v) the feasibility of lowering the 20 MW total rated thermal input thresholds; (vi) linkages between the EU ETS and other carbon markets; and (vii) carbon leakage protection measures for non-CBAM sectors. In addition, the consultant may be asked to carry out ad-hoc tasks related to the assessment of other interconnected elements that are to be included in the impact assessment. (3) Design, carry out and analyse the results of the public consultation on the evaluation and impact assessment of points 1 and 2.

title: Support for global mitigation modelling capacity in light of the just energy transition
description:
The outcome of the first Global Stocktake (GST), concluded at COP28, presents a clear guidance for the global just energy transition. It 1.) acknowledges that even the full implementation of the latest nationally determined contributions (NDCs) leaves a significant gap towards limiting global warming to 1.5 degrees, 2.) underscores that the impacts of climate change will be much lower at the temperature increase of 1.5 °C compared with 2 °C and resolves to pursue efforts to limit the temperature increase to 1.5 °C, 3.) notes that feasible, effective and low-cost mitigation options are already available in all sectors to keep 1.5 °C within reach in this critical decade with the necessary cooperation on technologies and support, and 4.) recognizes that limiting global warming to 1.5°C with no or limited overshoot requires deep, rapid and sustained reductions in global greenhouse gas emissions of 43 per cent by 2030 and 60 per cent by 2035 relative to the 2019 level and reaching net zero carbon dioxide emissions by 2050. 

The GST decision therefore calls on all Parties in paragraph 28 to engage in various actions in the energy sector to contribute to global efforts towards deep, rapid and sustained reductions in greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in line with 1.5°C pathways. It further notes that mitigation efforts embedded within the wider development context can increase the pace, depth and breadth of emissions reductions, as well as that policies that shift development pathways towards sustainability can broaden the portfolio of available mitigation responses and enable the pursuit of synergies with development objectives. 

This procurement therefore aims to take forward the strong call of the GST for significant action in the energy sector, and to reflect upon recent dynamics on global energy markets, especially related to price dynamics, fossil fuel subsidies, supply chain disruptions and the risk of stranded assets in the fossil fuels sector. The project shall provide and enhance the analytical base to address the urgent need to cut emissions in the energy sector (including all scopes of the energy sector, e.g., the heat and power, fuel production, industrial use , transport, etc.), in particular through the scale-up of renewables, the corresponding phase out of fossil fuels and the acceleration of energy efficiency improvements. It should further consider the role of different energy carriers, e.g., RFNBOs but also biofuels and biomass. The project shall create and provide insights into current emission pathways considering announced pledges and pathways under a 1.5°C scenario as well as contribute to enhancing ambition in domestic mitigation pathways. The project shall contribute to the mitigation pathway knowledge on a regional, national, and sub-national level and aims to close existing knowledge and capacity gaps linked to creating this modelling-based analysis in selected developing and emerging countries, primarily big emitters. The project shall further highlight and strengthen the link between mitigation action in the energy sector and just transition considerations, providing the socioeconomic credibility of modelled pathways necessary to implement the just energy transition and based on extensive in-country experience of project partners. As a result, in-country teams should be equipped to contribute to robust and ambitious climate action, for instance the development of future NDCs and Long-Term Strategies (LTSs) for low-carbon development, and use the created capacity to enhance the mitigation ambition compared to the status quo, especially through accelerating the just energy transition and by providing a robust foundation taking into consideration domestic just transition action. These outcomes shall further contribute to the preparation of the second Global Stock Take that will be concluded in 2028.

title: Support to the Commission for the assessment of submitted National Implementation Measures
description:
Directive 2003/87/EC (the EU ETS Directive) has been revised for the allocation period 2026 to 2030. In September 2024, Member States will have to submit to the Commission the list of installations covered by the Directive, as well as any free allocation for the period 2026 to 2030 for each installation in the list, calculated in accordance with Union-wide harmonised free allocation rules.

The data collected, referred to as National Implementation Measures (NIMs), must be verified and assessed by the Member States and thereafter submitted to the Commission in September 2024 that will, in turn, perform an assessment to determine compliance with the relevant legal provisions. 

Given the technical nature of the assessment, the amount of numbers that must be checked, the complexity of the free allocation rules, the formal and informal communication with the Member States and the short timeframe for concluding this work, as well as our previous experience, we foresee the need for support from a contractor for carrying out the assessment of the data. This will be extremely time-consuming work and also very important, as free allocation will have a financial impact on the participating companies. Moreover, it will be crucial to ensure comparably robust data across Member States, so a thorough assessment will need to be performed.

Analytical capacity based on greenhouse gas emissions modelling is providing the foundation to overcome both ambition and implementation gaps as it contributes to a knowledge base necessary to design impactful climate policies and regulation. Continuous modelling capacity is therefore required to answer the urgent call to increase climate action before 2030 and analyse new NDCs as well as new and updated long-term strategies for low carbon development (LT-LEDS), aiming at CO2 neutrality around 2050. The contracting authority requires access to state-of-the-art analytical capacity on global climate change mitigation action, as well as quantitative analysis and model-derived scenarios of global climate change mitigation.

title: Technical support for monitoring HFC price and phase-down evolution as a result of EU policies
description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure. 
Regulation (EU) No 517/2014 on fluorinated greenhouse gases foresees a phase-down of the supply of hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs) to the EU market. This phase-down has led to increased prices for these gases and a dynamic market situation which needs to be monitored and analysed. The purchase is to support DG CLIMA in monitoring of the effects of Regulation (EU) No 517/2014 in particular with respect to the functioning and impacts of the quota system, including potential future developments of that system.

title: Assessment of the first years of the functioning of the new allocation system based on benchmarks.
description: The EU emissions trading system (EU ETS), launched in 2005, is a cornerstone of the European Union's policy to combat climate change and its key tool for reducing industrial greenhouse gas emissions cost-effectively.A major revision was approved in 2009 in order to strengthen the system. The third phase of EU ETS, running from 2013 to 2020, has brought significant changes as compared to phases 1 and 2. Since 2013 the EU ETS is based on rules which are far more harmonised than before.The study is to document the impact of the benchmark-based harmonised allocation system on European industry. The aim is also to assess if the rules applicable in the third phase of EU ETS have changed the behaviour and trade and investment patterns of the industries covered by the ETS.

title: Shifting private finance towards climate-friendly investments.
description: The study will assess the amount of public finance that would be needed to shift investments towards climate-friendly investments looking into the 2 periods 'up to 2020' and then also '2020–2030', taking into account the effects of different framework and policy conditions.The study will:i) identify the key factors in a well-developed regulatory framework that can create the right incentives for private sector involvement without burdening public resources;ii) describe the financial instruments that can best leverage private resources;iii) from the perspective of institutional investors, analyse the current list of financial instruments, highlighting the pro/cons of the instruments and propose concrete enhancements of instruments needed to attract more institutional investors;iv) advise on the recommended role of the public sector, governments and public banks, in catalysing private sector investments in climate change; andv) explore the role that the EU budget can play to mobilise low carbon investments.

title: Multi-model Analysis Exercise on the Transformation of the Energy System
description: The general objective of the project is to perform a multi-model analysis of the evolution of EU energy system in the period 2030-2050, studying specifically at the required transformations in terms of energy demand and supply to 2040 on the path toward the 2050 economy-wide carbon neutrality objective. The project will:1. harmonise the assumptions retained in the different energy system models allowing for comparability;2. design and implement a modelling protocol to evaluate the required transformations in the different segments of the EU energy system (demand, supply, transformation); and3. deliver a quantitative multi-model analysis and detailed reporting of models’ outputs.The project will complement and strengthen DG CLIMA's modelling capacity and support the assessment of the 2040 intermediate climate target to be proposed in the first half of 2024 as per the European Climate Law.

title: Modelling of European climate policies.
description: The general objective of the contract is to make available updated and improved quantitative tools and to use them to assess scenarios and policy options for the implementation of the 2030 framework for climate and energy policies and climate-relevant elements of the Energy Union as well as other sectoral policies in the medium (up to 2030) and long term (to 2050 and if possible beyond), including economic, environmental and social implications, both for the EU as a whole as well as all its individual Member States and candidate countries. Specific objectives are:1. updating/constructing a reference projection and variants thereof;2. modelling policy scenarios and assessment of the impacts of measures or packages of climate or climate-relevant policy measures and their interactions;3. user-friendly presentation of models, assumptions and detailed (draft) reference results in consultation processes with Member States.

title: Supporting the impact assessment on the effects of mid- and long-term IMO climate measures on the Pacific Island countries, and advancing effective partnerships in IMO climate change related meetings
description: This action aims to support ambitious climate action in IMO by strengthening the Pacific Island States (PIS) in the organisation and their effective co-operation with the EU. The objective is to enable PIS to prepare for and participate in IMO, so they can actively support an ambitious revision of the IMO GHG strategy and contribute to the assessment of mid- and long-term IMO climate measures. For this, the project will fund a study to identify and analyse data on PIS which will be used to assess the impacts of future measures. A shortage of data from the region complicates the assessment of the effects of the measures, which the study will remedy. Secondly, this project will organise regional workshops and high-level meetings to facilitate shared EU-Pacific position in the negotiations on IMO, and provide technical assistance for PIS. The meetings will take place in 2023 and 2024. The action supports existing and successful EU-Pacific co-operation.

title: Support to the Development of Monitoring, Reporting and Verification Modalities, Procedures and Guidelines under the UNFCCC and to the Participation by the EU in UNFCCC Technical Reviews
description: The first objective is to support the EU in international climate negotiations related to transparency issues. This is to be achieved through provision of support to the commission for the development of modalities, procedures and guidelines as agreed under Art 13 of the Paris Agreement and in Katowice Rulebook, during a period of 2 years. The contractor is expected to prepare several papers, background materials and analyses and support the commission by participating in a number of expert meetings. The contractor is expected to support the commission in the effective implementation of the MRV arrangements under the UNFCCC, in particular the multilateral assessment and the facilitative sharing of views.The second objective is to provide support to the participation by the EU in selected UNFCCC technical reviews, during a period of 4 years. This will require that experts employed by the contractor will participate in and pass a UNFCCC examination to become review experts.

title: Assessment of EU climate policies in a EU mid-century perspective.
description: The objective is to make available quantitative (modelling) tools and apply these to assess options for future EU climate and energy policy. This entails the assessment of economic, environmental and social impacts for the EU and individual Member States. State-of-the-art models are to be used, and these have to be updated where needed and their integration needs to be ensured. A baseline projection and variants thereof need to be constructed. The effects of possible climate and energy policies including those related to non-energy greenhouse gas emissions such as those from land use, agriculture, waste and industrial sectors will need to be assessed. Finally, information needs to be exchanged in an interactive process with Member State experts and stakeholders. The modelling has to cover all EU Member States individually, candidate countries (and where possible other European countries). All sectors emitting greenhouse gas emissions have to be covered.

description: Review of guidance documents under Directive 2009/31/EC on the geological storage of carbon dioxide. (CLIMA.C2.6/MP2022). The four guidance documents on the implementation of Directive 2009/31/EC on the geological storage of carbon dioxide were developed more than 10 years ago. They are to be considered outdated due to the market related and technological changes. Given the growing market interest in the CCUS technologies, partially driven by the launch of the Innovation Fund and the Fit for 55 package, around 30 new CCUS projects are to be implemented in the Union by 2030. There is an urgent need to update the Guidance documents to facilitate the realisation of such projects.

title: Enhanced sharing of good practices on greenhouse gas emissions modelling between EU and Asian countries
description: Climate governance requires the ability to plan and implement national plans, policies and measures consistent with global goals including those of the Paris Agreement. There are no pathways to reaching globally agreed climate targets without major-emitting emerging Asian economies (as well as other G20 economies) taking significant steps towards climate neutrality.With this in mind, the action intends to reinforce global climate change mitigation effort by supporting developing countries’ experts work on national and sectoral GHG emissions modelling, strengthen capacity building for GHG emissions modelling and exchange of best practices and know-how between leading EU and Asian modellers (including China and India), working closely with government.This action builds on past and existing international cooperation and will seek to engage the most influential Asian/EU experts on models and modelling tools to increase domestic capacities on low-emission development scenarios modelling

title: Resource efficiency policies for land-use-related climate mitigation.
description: The objective of the study is to recommend a policy framework suited to optimise the reduction of land-use-related greenhouse gas emissions and to simultaneously maximise carbon removals, by promoting 4 major mitigation options in a coherent and consistent way, while preventing negative spillover effects. These 4 options imply the use of the land for biomass production for fossil energy substitution, material/product substitution related to harvested wood products and other biomaterials/biochemicals, and to use the land in a way which increases the overall stocks of terrestrial carbon in soils, above and below ground living biomass, and in litter/dead organic matter. Effective implementation of the policy framework should be envisaged to take place over the period until 2030.

title: Supporting Study for the Implementation of the ETS Directive and MRV Requirements for Maritime Transport
description: This procurement should support the Commission to fulfil its reporting requirements under Article 21(4) of Regulation (EU) 2015/757 by supporting the preparation of the three annual reports based on MRV data for the years 2023, 2024 and 2025. It should also support stakeholders in the implementation of the Regulation and the application of the ETS Directive to maritime by supporting the Commission in developing guidance documents. It should also assist the Commission in the preparation of an impact assessment for the review of the Regulation in accordance with its Article 22a, inter alia, to include within its scope ships below 5 000 gross tonnage but not below 400 and other aspects to be defined by the Commission. This procurement should support the Commission in monitoring the implementation and impacts of the ETS extension to maritime transport, in particular to detect evasive behaviour and considering outermost regions (in accordance with Article 3gg(3) of the ETS Directive).

title: VECTO Software and Code Development for the Next Amendment of Commission Regulation (EU) 2017/2400
description: VECTO is at the core of the system to determine CO2 emissions and energy consumption from heavy-duty vehicles (HDVs). It is the crucial tool for the implementation/development of CO2 emission standards for heavy-duty vehicles, contributing to the European Green Deal. VECTO is the backbone of the certification of HDVs and an essential tool to ensure the implementation and revision of the HDVs CO2 emission standards for various types of vehicles (conventional, hybrids, electric). It must be updated regularly to capture all latest technologies and developments in the automotive sector. This contract aims to further develop the code of the tool and bring up to a certain level all features needed for the next amendment of Commission Regulation (EU) 2017/2400. The contract will update the tool with certain technologies but also the VECTO VTP (Verification Testing Procedure) mode. It will also provide further technical support (software code maintenance) and users assistance via a helpdesk.

title: Study on mapping the development of the international carbon market.
description:
The objective of this study is to map out possible scenario(s) for the development of the global carbon market in the period 2020–2030 in light of the Paris Agreement and in particular its Article 6. Specifically, the study is to:
1. identify existing and planned carbon units/offset credits, including (voluntary) offset programmes around the globe;
2. assess the carbon units/offset credits identified under task 1 in terms of climate mitigation; and
3. elaborate and assess different options for the transfer, accounting and tracking of internationally transferred mitigation outcomes under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement.

title: Contract for the joint procurement of an auction monitor.
description: Pursuant to Article 24 of the Commission Regulation (EU) No 1031/2010 ('Auctioning Regulation'), the Commission and the Member States must appoint jointly an auction monitor. The joint procurement process is carried out pursuant to a joint action under Article 104(1) of Regulation (EU, Euratom) No 966/2012 and a joint procurement procedure under Article 133(c) of Regulation (EU, Euratom) No 1268/2012, and under the Joint Procurement Agreement to procure an auction monitor entered into by the Commission and the Member States (http://ec.europa.eu/clima/policies/ets/cap/auctioning/documentation_en.htm).The auction monitor will be entrusted with monitoring and reporting tasks provided for in Article 25 of the Auctioning Regulation; in particular, it will monitor the auctions taking place on all auction platforms, and report on the proper implementation of the auctions to the Commission on behalf of the Member States and to the Member States concerned.

description: The main objective of this (recurrent) project is to support the Commission and Member States in the further implementation of harmonized and cost-effective EU ETS monitoring, reporting verification and accreditation (MRVA), during 2024-2025.Specific objectives are to:• provide Secretariat support to the EU ETS Compliance Forum in 2024 and 2025, maintaining an effective platform for discussion and cooperation between Member States and the Commission, including in the Task Force setting, and the well-functioning of the EU ETS MRVA system;• provide support to the Commission concerning the maintenance of MRVA guidance, templates and other tools published by the Commission in support of the MRR and AVR;• provide additional support in relation to ad hoc technical enquiries on EU ETS MRVA issues.Work under this contract shall take into account the revised EU ETS Directive and the revision of the legal acts, in particular MRR and AVR.

title: Climate-ADAPT: new tools and functionalities developing the EU strategy on adaptation to climate change.
description: This service contract envisages the development of new tools and functionalities for the Web-based European climate adaptation platform (http://climate-adapt.eea.europa.eu/), 'Climate-ADAPT', building on the current version of the platform.The project aims at developing the concept of 'one-stop shop', as stated in the EU strategy on adaptation to climate change, by developing tools and improving the sections holding information from different geographical scales (national, regional, subnational). In particular, a new subsection of the platform should be developed for the integration of the EU urban adaptation initiative (mayors adapt); also, solutions for better presenting and interacting with the information on countries and regions need to be developed.Additionally, the contract aims at improving the platform's usability by making it more user-friendly and structurally coherent, including developing tools to enhance the interaction of the platform's users and managers.

title: Framework contract for services in the field of analysis, assessment and policy development in relation to climate-forcing impacts of light-duty road vehicles.
description: Regulation (EC) No 443/2009 (CO2 from cars) sets out a short-term target of 130 g CO2/km to be achieved by manufacturers of passenger cars by 2015 with a phase-in beginning in 2012. A long-term target of 95 g CO2/km has been specified for 2020. Regulation (EU) No 510/2011 (CO2 from vans) sets out a target of 175 g CO2/km to be achieved by manufacturers of vans by 2017. A long-term target of 147 g CO2/km has been specified for 2020.A number of subsequent implementing measures have been adopted to enact various elements of these Regulations.Article 13(5) of Regulation (EC) No 443/2009 requires that the specific emissions targets and the derogations for low volume and niche manufacturers shall be reviewed with the aim of defining:— the modalities for reaching, by the year 2020, a long-term target of 95 g CO2/km in a cost-effective manner, and— the aspects of the implementation of that target, including the excess emissions premium.In parallel, Article 13(1) of Regulation (EU) No 510/2011 establishes similar requirements and requires the achievability of the target to be confirmed.The Commission is currently carrying out reviews of Regulations (EC) No 443/2009 (CO2 in cars) and (EU) 510/2011 (CO2 from vans) which should be completed by the end of 2012. There may be a need for ad hoc support with respect to the adoption procedure in the European Parliament and Council. Further support might be needed in relation to any implementation or monitoring that is or might be required. Requirements could also arise in relation to further policy development. Examples could include any subsequent reviews of the legislation, the need to address any possible interaction between the van legislation and any future strategy on heavy-duty vehicles or possible future action relating to powered two-wheelers or quadricycles.This body of legislation and policies is expected to be periodically reviewed to take account of the evolving scientific information. In addition, EU policies must also undergo continuous assessment to evaluate their effectiveness and correct implementation, particularly with respect to attainment of the EU's objectives with respect to climate change. The successful tenderers will be expected to provide services in connection with the following:(1) analytical support in relation to climate-forcing emissions from vehicles and the energy life cycle, principally CO2;(2) analysis of specific aspects of current EU road vehicle CO2 legislation and its implementing measures and aspects that might be subject to change; (3) technologies, costs, benefits, cost effectiveness, supply constraints, price premia, other economic impacts and other implications of measures to reduce climate-forcing emissions from vehicles;(4) insight on past vehicle market changes as regards evolution in vehicle segments, equipment provided, cost, technical aspects, manufacturers' offer, consumer preferences, impact on climate-forcing emissions; (5) analysis and assessment relating to likely future changes in technical aspects, market trends, developments in consumer demand and manufacturer offer; (6) support on policy development for emissions and energy labelling of vehicles at point of sale and the implementation of relevant EU legislation;(7) advice on issues related to the emissions of conventional air pollutants from vehicles and their interaction with climate-forcing emissions;(8) technical and legal advice on issues relating to vehicle type approval procedures;(9) ad hoc information and advice on other aspects of motor vehicle markets, technology and environmental impacts;(10) global trade and competitiveness implications of EU vehicle standards to reduce climate-forcing emissions.

title: Analytical Capacity for International Climate Action (Renewable)
description: GHG emissions need to be reduced by 43 % in 2030 compared to 2019 levels to keep a 1,5-degree pathway in reach. The gap in emission reductions until 2030 and beyond is both a challenge of raising ambition as well as realising implementation. Analytical capacity based on greenhouse gas emissions modelling is providing the foundation to overcome both ambition and implementation gaps as it contributes to a knowledge base necessary to design impactful climate policies and regulation. Continuous modelling capacity is therefore required to answer the urgent call to increase climate action before 2030 and analyse new NDCs as well as new and updated long-term strategies for low carbon development (LT-LEDS), aiming at CO2 neutrality around 2050. The contracting authority requires access to state-of-the-art analytical capacity on global climate change mitigation action, as well as quantitative analysis and model-derived scenarios of global climate change mitigation.

title: Study on climate benefits of material substitution by forest biomass and harvested wood products: perspective 2030.
description: The overall objective of this study is to provide reliable data and analysis on the overall climate change mitigation potential associated with harvested wood products (HWPs). The time-framing of the study will be 1960–2030, in order to inform future EU and Member States' policies related to climate change mitigation in relevant activities. It will also address a series of sub-objectives such as: identifying further research needs; investigating the demand and supply of biomass type (hardwood, softwood, etc.); understanding carbon flows associated with HWP; establishing a clear methodology for assessing cascade life cycles.

title: Mainstreaming of climate change into rural development policy post 2013.
description: The primary objective of this study is to deliver technical guidance and guidelines for managing authorities in Member States, namely:— an inventory, listing and detailing characteristics of new and innovative types of operations (regionally differentiated adaptation and mitigation operations):o to fit under rural development measures, specifically prioritising and addressing climate objectives,o and demonstrating a contribution to the EU's 'green growth' priorities,— recommendations and examples on how to address climate change in other rural development instruments, such as the Leader instrument and cooperation measure (Article 36 of the Regulation),— examples of relevant combinations of measures for each focus areas of the Union's rural development properties that are related to climate change,— criteria for assessment how to measure relevant combinations of measures in view of their climate effects and contribution to progress towards green growth, in particular creation of jobs.A further objective of the contract is to assist the Commission in disseminating the study results by preparing outreach tools and supporting a workshop.

title: Audit of the annual accounts of the Innovation Fund for the years ending 31/12/2020 and 31/12/2021
description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure. 
As per the article 23 of the Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/856, “The Commission shall prepare annual accounts of the Innovation Fund for each financial year, which shall run from 1 January to 31 December on the basis of the financial statements provided pursuant to the first subparagraph. Those accounts shall be subject to an independent external audit.” In order to comply with the Regulation, DG CLIMA needs technical assistance services to conduct the audit of the Innovation Fund financial statements for the years 2020 and 2021.

title: Support for developing the type approval of hydrogen internal combustion engines (H2 ICE) for HDV applications.
description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure. 
Objectives and tasks

Currently H2 ICEs HDV cannot be type-approved yet for their pollutant emissions and fuel consumption. This makes the marketing of these engines on a larger scale impossible. In addition, such emissions type-approval is a precondition for including HDVs operated with H2 ICEs into VECTO simulations. The latter task is currently being developed under a different contract by the Technical University of Graz (TUG) and should be finalised until the end of 2022.

The Commission therefore has launched already in 2019 a task force preparing amendments to UNECE Regulation 49 in this respect. The work has been interrupted due to the COVID pandemic since vehicle testing was not possible for a certain period, but has been relaunched in July 2021. The JRC, in collaboration with several vehicle, engine and test equipment manufacturers, is now leading a specific programme validating the relevant existing test procedures of UNECE R 49, which were essentially developed for diesel vehicles, for their application to H2 ICEs.

The purpose of this contract is to prepare the necessary amendments to UNECE Regulation 49 as a formal document to be submitted to UNECE, in particular on the basis of the following elements:
‒	A first draft proposed by ACEA, which needs to be revised and critically assessed in close collaboration with the Commission
‒	Input from the test validation program led by the JRC
‒	The work for integrating H2 ICE vehicles into VECTO performed by TUG, e.g. for defining the requirements on H2 fuel consumption measurements 
and possibly other sources.

The holder of the contract shall discuss the resulting draft document and finalise it with a group of stakeholders that will be constituted and conveyed by the Commission. Given the current situation it can be assumed that all meetings will take place online. The necessary communication tools and the online platform for exchanging documents (Circabc) will be made available by the Commission.
The holder of the contract will also provide technical support for the processing of the amendments to R 49 at UNECE to the extent it is necessary, which will be compensated on a per-use basis.

title: Support on Devising a Carbon Removal Certification Mechanism
description: Some carbon removal methods, including land-based solutions, and Carbon Capture and Utilization (CCU) may have the capacity, under certain conditions, to contribute to the decarbonisation of the economy.In order to provide appropriate support to the relevant carbon removal methods, a possible solution would be to design a certification mechanism that is able to establish the volume of carbon removals or savings. This certification mechanism should also ensure technology neutrality, avoid double-counting of emissions, ensure liability and address the permanence of the carbon sequestration.Such a certification mechanism would require a stringent process and a governance compatible with robust greenhouse gases inventories. Support is needed to analyse different options and provide different appropriate solutions for this mechanism to work properly.
